correctness.rationale: For finite K_{a,b}, each A-A walk compresses into core two-step segments of cost at least M_{ij}; conversely concatenated argmin segments attain the metric closure, giving exact equality. At one peripheral vertex, P(two-spoke sum<=t/sqrt b)=t²/(2b)+O(b^{-3/2}), and overlap of two distinct pair events is O(b^{-3/2}) since at least three independent spokes are small. Independence across b periphery sites yields joint upper-orthant convergence to a product Rayleigh survival function; finite-dimensional path closure is continuous. For a marked periphery vertex, W=min_a Exp(1) is Exp(a), and distances lie between W and W+core diameter, similarly two marks W_l+W_h and +diameter. Excluding finitely many tags leaves asymptotically the same Rayleigh pair minima and independent marks; chance a tagged vertex changes scaled pair minima is O(1/b). Reconstructed the proof and independently checked core closure/peripheral inequalities on 384 random integer-weight graph instances.
